title: Astronomers Create Gallery of 16 ‘Cosmic Gems’ to Show Variety of Shapes a Galaxy Can Be
text:
Space scientists have put together a photo gallery of ‘cosmic gems’ to showcase the variety of sizes, shapes, and high-energy features of distant galaxies.

Astronomers put galaxies into three main categories: spirals like our own Milky Way with arms emanating from their cores, ellipticals that are older and likely the results of mergers, and irregulars that can encompass a wide range of galactic phenomena.

Each one of the 16 new pictures contain X-ray telescope data from NASA’s Chandra Observatory collected across decades of operation. (See the gallery in full, here.)

That high-energy data has been combined with data from space telescopes like Webb and Hubble, as well as several other arrays both on the ground and in space—including the IXPE (Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer), Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, and NuSTAR (Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope Array).

NASA says that studying galaxies offers a way to learn about our own.

“Galaxies are like cosmic gems, each with characteristics including size and shape that make them distinct,” says Megan Watzke of the Chandra X-ray Center.

“Just as gems reveal the history of Earth through how they were forged over billions of years, these galactic gems are a way to study Earth’s place in our home galaxy of the Milky Way.
